ai.description: *Uropeltis grandis* is a stout, cylindrical snake reaching 30–40 cm. It is dark brown with yellow lateral spots and possesses a distinct, heavily keeled, truncated tail shield used for burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis grandis* is distinguished by its unique, large, shield-like terminal scale that is abruptly truncated and deeply bicarinate, unlike the smoother tails of others.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis grandis* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis grandis* is a fossorial specialist that spends most of its life underground, emerging to the surface primarily during or after heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis grandis* is viviparous, giving birth to live young. While specific clutch sizes and breeding seasons remain poorly documented, they typically produce small litters.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis grandis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests above 1,500 meters.
